name: Choroidal Osteoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Choroidal Osteoma

criteria.description: Presence of a yellow-white, slightly elevated, well-demarcated choroidal lesion on fundoscopic examination
High reflectivity with acoustic shadowing on B-scan ultrasonography consistent with calcified lesion
Computed tomography demonstrating hyperdense choroidal lesion confirming ossification
Early hyperfluorescence with late staining on fluorescein angiography

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic fundoscopic lesion plus confirmatory imaging with B-scan ultrasound or CT scan
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; biopsy is rarely indicated.

pathognomonic.notes: Visible on fundoscopic exam, hallmark of disease
searchTerms: yellow-white raised spot in eye choroid
visual changes due to eye abnormality

occasional.symptomName: Retinal pigment epithelial atrophy adjacent to lesion
searchTerms: thinning of retinal pigment epithelium adjacent to lesion
retina detaching secondary to other eye problems
retinal detachment caused by underlying condition
new abnormal blood vessels under retina rupturing

rare.symptomName: Severe vision loss progressing to blindness
searchTerms: severe loss of vision leading to blindness

imaging: B-scan ultrasonography showing highly reflective choroidal lesion with acoustic shadowing
CT scan demonstrating hyperdense ossified lesion in choroid
Fluorescein angiography with early hyperfluorescence and late staining
other: Fundoscopic exam revealing yellow-white, slightly elevated, well-demarcated lesion in posterior pole

distinguishingFeatures: Low to medium reflectivity on B-scan ultrasound
Usually associated with systemic causes such as hypercalcemia
Diffuse calcification rather than localized lesion
Lack of typical fundoscopic appearance of osteoma

references: Gass JD. Stereoscopic Atlas of Macular Diseases: Diagnosis and Treatment. 4th ed. 1997.
Shields CL, Shields JA. Choroidal Osteoma: Clinical Features and Management. Ophthalmology. 2001;108(3):586-595.
